summary: A solid paper with good IELTS-style traps in Parts 1-3 and a park map that matches the directions exactly. All answer keys are correct. Two things to note: the street name in Q5 is never spelled out, which is unfair in a Part 1, and Parts 1 and 4 are on the short side (about 510 and 630 words).
strengths: Part 1 corrections are natural (five -> seven years, hose -> door, Monday -> Wednesday) and the booking reference uses the real 'W for window' technique.
Part 2 map task has rejected locations built in (drinks station not at the north end of the lake; photographer not at the north-east corner), and the SVG matches every direction.
Part 3 is a natural two-student discussion with each wrong option raised and argued away.
Part 4 notes follow the lecture in order with single concrete nouns as answers.

issues.problem: Q5 'Bustan' (street name) is never spelled out in the script. In a real Part 1 an unfamiliar name is always spelled; students cannot be sure of 'Bustan' vs 'Bostan'.
issues.change: The caller now spells B-U-S-T-A-N; Bostan stays accepted. Re-recorded with ElevenLabs, 2026-11-10.

issues.problem: The explanations for Q29 and Q30 swapped the speakers: it is Laylo who will email her old primary school, and Jasur who will write the sample questions.
issues.change: Corrected Q29 and Q30 explain in the overlay.

issues.problem: Part 4 is about 630 words and its notes repeat the lecture closely (e.g. 'punished by ___', 'sits on a ___ filled with wool'), so it is slightly easier than a real Part 4.
issues.change: Part 4 extended to about 800 words with distractors (answers unchanged) and re-recorded with ElevenLabs, 2026-11-10.

issues.problem: Part 1 script is about 510 words, shorter than a typical real Part 1.
issues.change: Part 1 extended to real length with natural exchanges and distractors (answers unchanged) and re-recorded with ElevenLabs, 2026-11-10.
